clue.text: Stale wind sends American packing

indicators.note: to send someone packing is to dismiss them, so those letters are told to leave

parts.note: flatus is the medical word for wind in the gut
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone's stale wind is so bad that an American visitor runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator phrase 'sends ... packing' is split around the piece it removes, so the American is taken out of the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer or air that has gone stale has lost its fizz and freshness, a common adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Legal proceeding supports fine for splinter group

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that supports another sits underneath it, fixing the order of the pieces

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a lawsuit is an action at law

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is backed as a good way to deal with a breakaway group.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so the legal proceeding supports, i.e. sits below, the F for fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a small dissenting group that has broken away within a larger party or body.

clue.text: Where veggies might not grow in difficult times

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a poor plot of garden soil
second meaning: a spell of trouble, as in going through one

explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase is read literally as a poor piece of ground, then idiomatically as a rough period in someone's life.
explanation.definitionFit: People say they are going through a rough stretch or unhappy period using this idiom about a poor plot.

clue.text: Tiger possibly stalking hind in the bush?

indicators.note: a stalker follows behind its quarry, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: hind means rear, as in the back legs
Tiger Woods, the golfer, is one person with this surname

explanation.surface: A big cat hunts a female deer through the scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiger and hind look like predator and prey, a deer; instead Tiger is the golfer and hind means rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote wild country far from towns is called the bush or the backwoods, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Society girl rejected having sex in sleeping bag?

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society
a roll in the hay is slang for sex

explanation.surface: A socialite turns down a romp in a sleeping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reads as the girl saying no, but it turns her letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroll is bedding rolled up for carrying when camping, close to a sleeping bag in use.

clue.text: One might take these at university for starters?

definitions.text: One might take these at university
definitions.meaning: first meaning: programmes of study a student signs up for
second meaning: parts of a meal, a starter being the first one

explanation.walkthrough: 'For starters' reads as 'to begin with', but starters are an example of the second meaning, parts of a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Students enrol on programmes of study, and a meal is served in stages, with appetisers first.

clue.text: Sleep is one method to get fresh for the most part

definitions.note: Sleep is a surname here, so the definition names the first name that goes with it

indicators.note: most but not all of a word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a way of doing something is a method
fresh means new, as in fresh ideas

explanation.surface: A tip on the best way to wake up refreshed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Sleep is a famous British ballet dancer, so the capital on Sleep is a surname, not a start-of-sentence capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The dancer's full name is Wayne Sleep, so the first name belongs to one well-known person named Sleep.

clue.text: Old lady chasing old boy and a former leader

indicators.note: whatever is chasing runs behind, so this piece goes after the others

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
taken as written
one's old lady is slang for one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: An elderly woman pursues a retired man and an ex-politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'former leader' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'former leader' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama served as US president until 2017, so he is an ex-head of state.

clue.text: Has beer ruined grizzly female?

indicators.note: something ruined is broken apart, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Has drink spoilt a grumpy woman's mood?
explanation.walkthrough: Grizzly looks like 'grumpy' but is the kind of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A female of any bear species, including the grizzly, is called by this compound name.

clue.text: Junkie turned over European dude to get online identity

parts.note: a user is slang for a drug addict

indicators.note: to turn something over flips it, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a dude is a man

explanation.surface: An addict mugs a European man to steal his online account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' sounds like robbing someone; it reverses the European dude.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle you log in with on a website is the label that identifies you there.

clue.text: Tea given by empty officers' mess

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Tea is served in an officers' mess that has no one in it.
explanation.walkthrough: An officers' mess is a military dining room, but here 'mess' is the definition, a state of disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Total disorder and confusion is a mess, a straightforward synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Street of houses by railway in Arundel demolished

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside another
a demolished building is knocked down and its parts scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; Arundel is a town in Sussex
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Houses near the railway line in the town of Arundel are knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: Houses here are theatres: Drury Lane in London's West End is home to the Theatre Royal, one of the oldest playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street is famous for theatres, which are called houses in the trade, as in a full house.

clue.text: I'm so pure I must change to be tyrannical

indicators.note: a demand for change means the letters are rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A saint admits that such purity forces him to become a despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm so pure I' reads as a speaker's boast, but it is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone domineering and overbearing who expects obedience is described with either adjective.

clue.text: Duck seen in English Channel going wrong way!

indicators.note: travelling the wrong way means heading backwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Dave is a British TV channel showing comedy repeats

explanation.surface: A duck is spotted swimming the wrong way across the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Channel is the sea between England and France, but here the words split: Dave is a UK television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or blow is to dodge or avoid it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Sport drag, perhaps, at society dance

parts.note: a drag or dragnet is one kind of net pulled along the bottom
a ball is a formal dance held by society

explanation.surface: Someone shows off wearing drag at a posh dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a verb, to wear showily, and drag as cross-dressing; really it is the noun and a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game, played mostly in Britain and the Commonwealth, where players shoot a ball into a high hoop.

clue.text: One who's likely to ridicule small chest

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a person for having a small chest.
explanation.walkthrough: The chest looks like part of the body, but it is a box for valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock or jeer, so a person given to mocking is described by the agent noun.

clue.text: Live hornet buzzing around First Class

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece surrounds another
a buzzing insect flits about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means first class, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A living hornet is flying about in the first-class cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: Live looks like an adjective meaning alive, describing the hornet; it means being broadcast as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme being broadcast right now is described with this phrase, the radio and television sense.

clue.text: Do it and care not if given a kicking!

indicators.note: something kicked about is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Just go for it and don't worry if you get beaten up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do it' is a coy euphemism for having sex, which is why it can define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The euphemism refers to having sexual intercourse, especially outside marriage, which is the formal verb.

clue.text: A revolutionary way to save one hurting the most?

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safely held, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: taken as written
Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary
ST, street, is a way
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A radical method of rescuing the person in most pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The one goes inside the revolutionary's name, splitting it CH-E, before the way is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of achy describes whoever feels the most pain, matching the phrase exactly.

clue.text: Enliven originally apathetic nurse with one Bud

indicators.note: originally points to how things began, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of both words
I is the Roman numeral for one
bud, short for buddy, is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Cheer up a listless nurse by giving her a flower bud.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Bud makes it look like a beer or a flower bud; it is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring life and energy to something is to give it vigour, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Upset teacher bitten by hawk is one likely to take a holiday!

definitions.text: one likely to take a holiday

indicators.note: whatever is bitten sits between the jaws, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them, selling pushily

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir

explanation.surface: A teacher distressed after a bird attack decides to go on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawk suggests a bird of prey biting the teacher; it is the verb for selling in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller visiting places for pleasure is on vacation, so the description fits a sightseer.

clue.text: A naturist ultimately had lost interest in wearing clothes

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of a word counts

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
to have tired of something is to have lost interest

explanation.surface: A nudist finally got bored with going naked and put clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost interest in' seems one phrase, but 'in' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attired is dressed, so the past-participle adjective means having garments on.

clue.text: Do not cross any politicians on election day!

definitions.text: Do not cross any politicians on election day!

parts.note: surface reading: avoid angering anyone in politics
setter's reading: put no X beside any candidate on the ballot paper, i.e. decline to vote

explanation.walkthrough: Crossing a politician sounds like annoying them; on a ballot you mark your choice with a cross, so marking none means not voting.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from voting for any candidate is to hold back one's vote deliberately.

clue.text: Some cadre's Serbian chap who sorts out wounds?

indicators.note: some of something is only a part, so the letters lie inside a longer run

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A Serbian member of a military unit acts as its field medic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this dresser is a medical helper, not a piece of furniture or a theatre assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies bandages to injuries is named after that job, dressing wounds, an agent noun.

clue.text: Totally cool to have a couple of lines?

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them

explanation.surface: Someone thinks snorting a couple of lines would be really cool.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines hints at drugs or poetry; here it is just the letter L twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means altogether or in total, as when adding up a sum, so it matches the adverb.

clue.text: One who invests in The Guardian?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a backer who puts money into a theatre show or start-up
second meaning: a guardian spirit watching over someone

explanation.walkthrough: The italics make it look like the newspaper, so the clue reads as a shareholder in a paper; really a guardian is a protective spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre and business backers are called by this name, as is the protective heavenly being.

clue.text: Old red sheets one earl switched around

indicators.note: switching things means swapping their places, so one letter trades for another

parts.note: bed linen is sheets
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: Faded red bedsheets that an aristocrat turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I in the sheets for an E and the result is the Soviet founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin, leader of the Russian Revolution, was a communist, and red is a common label for communists.

clue.text: Nurse and I let loose, getting dirty

indicators.note: things let loose run free and scatter, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse and I let our hair down and get a bit filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like part of the indicator 'let loose', but it is fodder too; 'loose' alone does the shuffling work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not free from germs is contaminated or unclean, which is a close synonym.

clue.text: A chap at home visiting artist in the country

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so one piece enters another

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the stock artist
a gent is a man or chap
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A man staying at home goes to see a painter who lives in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' reads as the countryside, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America, so it is an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: I had touch of shame necking old man's tablets

indicators.note: to neck something is to swallow it down, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: a touch is only a trace of something, so just its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
one's old man is one's father, PA

explanation.surface: Someone feels a bit ashamed about swallowing their father's pills.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'old man' is 'is', linking wordplay to definition, not a possessive; tablets are computers, not pills.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPad is Apple's brand of touchscreen computer, so the plural names several such devices.

clue.text: Duke that wife will leave for another duke

indicators.note: whoever leaves is no longer present, so that letter drops out

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington, who defeated Napoleon at Waterloo
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A nobleman's wife walks out on him for a different duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke reads as a title both times, but the first Duke is the jazz bandleader Duke Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz composer Edward Ellington was known by his nickname, which is this title.

clue.text: A noble look

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of the nobility, such as a lord in the House of Lords
second meaning: to gaze closely or with difficulty

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a lofty glance, but it is two separate meanings: a titled person and to squint.
explanation.definitionFit: A British lord holds a peerage, and to squint or gaze searchingly at something is the verb.
